fullPassage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater (a) accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they (b) include information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the (c) quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is (d) morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to (e) escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.

✅ ② insulating — 'turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating'에서 숫자 변환이 도덕적으로 무감각하게 만든다는 문맥. 앞뒤로 고통을 전달하지 못한다는 내용이 이어지므로 insulating이 적절.
❌ ① suffering — '고통'은 통계가 말하지 못하는 대상이지, 숫자화의 특성은 아님.
❌ ③ accuracy — '정확성'은 앞부분 내용이고, 이 빈칸의 문맥과 맞지 않음.
❌ ④ distribution — '분배'는 소득 분배 맥락의 단어로, 이 빈칸과 무관.
det.tip: insulating은 '절연하는, 차단하는'이라는 뜻으로, morally insulating은 '도덕적으로 무감각하게 만드는'을 의미합니다.

questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater (a) accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they (b) include information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the (c) quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is (d) morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to (e) escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 젊은 학생들의 미래는 국가 시험 점수에 묶여 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① '젊은 학생들의 장래는 국가 시험 성적에 좌우된다' — 'the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests'와 일치.
❌ ② 글에서는 숫자가 언어보다 더 적절한 묘사 수단이 아니라고 함(no more appropriate).
